This application coming on for admission this day, the   the following:
 ORDER
This is a petition u/S.482 of Cr.P.C challenging the order of Magistrate whereby the application filed u/S.239 for discharge has been rejected.
Against the said order, the petitioners preferred a revision before the Addl. Sessions Judge, Sardarpur, District Dhar.

entities.text: Addl. Sessions Judge, Sardarpur, District Dhar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The said revision petition has also been dismissed.

As per the facts of the case, on 29.1.2021 an FIR was lodged by the respondent No.2 Sapna against the present petitioners alleging demand of dowry and harassment on which a case was registered at P.S. Sardarpur, District Dhar at Crime No. 51/2021 u/S.498A, 323, 504, 506 and 34 of IPC.
Counsel for petitioners submits that as per the contents of the FIR, no allegation of any physical assault has been made against the petitioners except the husband.
Omnibus allegations have been made against all the family members for demand of dowry and harassment.
The only allegation against the in-laws, brother-in-law and sister-in-law is that on their instigation the husband used to beat the complainant.

Upon perusal of the FIR, it is clear that a specific allegation has been made against all the petitioners for demand of dowry and on the said demand, it is stated that two times the father of the complainant had given amount to the petitioners.
At one time it is alleged that Rs.50,000/- has been given to the husband of the complainant and on second time Rupees thirteen lakhs were given to the husband.
It is alleged that the husband used to beat the complainant.

She has made specific allegation against all the petitioners i.e. husband Utsav, father-in-law Vipendra Kumar Chaturvedi,
mother-in-law Geeta, brother-in-law Ujwal @ Sahil and sister-in-law Surbhi for demand of dowry and causing mental and physical torture.
On their instigation the husband used to beat her.

The trial court, after considering the contents in the FIR and the material made available by the prosecution framed the charges u/Ss.498-A, 323, 504, 506/34 of IPC and Sec.3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

sentences.text: Counsel for petitioners submits that on the face value of FIR and the material collected by the prosecution, no case is made out for trial of the offence and the petitioners have been falsely implicated in the present case and, therefore, the petitioners cannot be put to trial on omnibus allegations.
He prays for quashment of the impugned orders, the FIR and the charges.

In support of his contentions, he has placed reliance on the judgments of Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana & Ors Vs. Bhajan Lal & Ors 1992 Supp(1) SCC 335, Preeti Gupta & another Vs. State of Jharkhand & another (2010) 7 SCC 667, Geeta Mehrotra & another Vs. State of UP & another (2012)
10 SCC 741, Kahkashan Kausar alias Sonam & Ors. Vs. State of Bihar & Ors. (2022) 6 SCC 599, Alok Lodhi & Ors. Vs. State of MP & another 2022 SCC OnLine MP 750 and Mirza Iqbal alias Golu &
another Vs. State of UP & another AIR 2022 SC 69 and orders passed by this Court in the matter of Prem Kumar & another Vs. State of MP & another passed in M.Cr.C. No.37680/2020 order dated 24.3.2021 and Gurmukha & Ors. Vs. State of MP & another passed in M.Cr.C. No.9413/2021 dated 27.10.2022.

sentences.text: After hearing learned counsel for parties and upon perusal of the FIR and the statement of the complainant and parents of the complainant, I find no illegality or perversity in the order for interfering in exercise of the powers u/S.482 Cr.P.C.
Moreover, it is trite to state that at the time of framing of charge, the material and quality of evidence cannot be gone into.
This Court is well aware about the limitation of the Court while exercising the revisional/inherent jurisdiction, which does not empower to intervene at an interlocutory stage.
Moreover, all that has to be looked into at the time of framing of charge is that whether there was existence of prima facie case.
So also it would be profitable to rely on State of M.P. Vs. S.B. Hohar and others reported in 2002(2) MPLJ 322, whereby the Court held thus :-

entities.text: State of M.P. Vs. S.B. Hohar and others reported in 2002(2) MPLJ 322
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "It is settled law that at the stage of framing the charge, the Court has to prima facie consider whether there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.
The Court is not required to appreciate the evidence and arrive at the conclusion that the material produced are sufficient or not for convicting the accused.
If the Court is satisfied that a prima facie case is made out for proceeding further, then a charge has to be framed."

In the matter of Umar Abdul Sakoor sorathia Vs Intelligence officer, Narcotic Control Bureau reported in (2000) 1 SCC 138 whereby the Supreme Court held thus :
"It is well settled that at the stage of framing charge, the Court is not expected to go deep into the probative value of the materials on record.

entities.text: Umar Abdul Sakoor sorathia Vs Intelligence officer, Narcotic Control Bureau reported in (2000) 1 SCC 138
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If on the basis of materials on record that Court could come to the conclusion that the accused would have committed the offence the Court is obliged to frame the charge and proceed to the trial."

In the matter of State of Maharashtra and others Vs. Som Nath Thapa and others reported in (1996)
4 SCC 659 whereby the Apex Court Court held thus :

sentences.text: "The aforesaid shows that if on the basis of materials on record, a Court could come to the conclusion that commission of the offence is probable consequence, a case for framing of charge exists.

To put it differently, it the Court were to think that the accused might have committed the offence it can frame the charge, though for conviction the conclusion is required to be that the accused has committed the offence.

It is apparent that at the stage of framing of a charge, probative value of the materials on record cannot be gone into; the materials brought on record by the prosecution has to be accepted as true at that stage."

The judgments relied upon by learned counsel for petitioners would not apply to the facts of the present case in view of the specific allegations made in the FIR and in the statement of the complainant and witnesses.
In view of the aforesaid, no case is made out for interference.
The petition is accordingly dismissed.
